# Purpose

This document uses the **77 core functions** of rSpacing (configuration, requests, runs, outputs, plots, weather files and run specifications) in operational order. The scenario API added in rSpacing 0.10.07-0.10.09 (`spacing_crop()`, `new_spacing_scenario()` and the management and rotation options) is covered, with automatic checks, by the cookbook `rSpacing_cookbook_v1.00_EN.Rmd`. Each function has a dedicated chunk. Operations that require the local APSIMx solution or a model run are protected by explicit checks.

Revision 10 (rSpacing 0.10.09, Spacing.Tool2 0.09.10) uses the shared workspace with sibling `rSpacing/` and `apsim/` repositories. By default, `params$run_models` is `false`: the manual documents and checks package functions without starting APSIMx. Set `run_models: true` explicitly for the integration test. The request keeps `mock = TRUE`, so `Spacing.Tool2` and APSIMx are executed without requiring the remote data service. Runs, results, and logs are written only under the corresponding workspace directories.

**What the `setup` chunk does.** It prepares the rendering environment, loads rSpacing, sets global parameters, and determines whether model runs can be executed. The chunk produces no visible output, but creates the objects shared by all subsequent sections.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6, dpi = 150
)

stopifnot(requireNamespace("rSpacing", quietly = TRUE))
if (utils::packageVersion("rSpacing") < numeric_version("0.10.9")) {
  stop(
    "This report requires rSpacing 0.10.09 or later. Installed version: ",
    as.character(utils::packageVersion("rSpacing"))
  )
}
library(rSpacing)
DOCUMENT_STARTED_AT <- Sys.time()
MODEL_RUN_ELAPSED_SECONDS <- NA_real_

RUN_MODELS <- isTRUE(params$run_models)
BUILD_CONFIGURATION <- as.character(params$build_configuration)
TARGET_FRAMEWORK <- as.character(params$target_framework)

# All paths are derived from one shared root. The value ".." is
# correct when this Rmd is executed from the workflows/ directory.
WORKSPACE_ROOT <- normalizePath(
  params$workspace_root,
  winslash = "/",
  mustWork = TRUE
)
RSPACING_ROOT <- normalizePath(
  file.path(WORKSPACE_ROOT, "rSpacing"),
  winslash = "/",
  mustWork = TRUE
)
SPACING_ROOT <- normalizePath(
  file.path(WORKSPACE_ROOT, "apsim"),
  winslash = "/",
  mustWork = TRUE
)

OUTPUT_SUBDIR <- as.character(params$output_subdir)
if (!nzchar(OUTPUT_SUBDIR) || grepl("/", OUTPUT_SUBDIR, fixed = TRUE) || grepl("\\", OUTPUT_SUBDIR, fixed = TRUE)) {
  stop("params$output_subdir must be one non-empty directory name.")
}
WORK_ROOT <- file.path(WORKSPACE_ROOT, "runs", OUTPUT_SUBDIR)
OUTPUT_ROOT <- file.path(WORKSPACE_ROOT, "results", OUTPUT_SUBDIR)
LOG_ROOT <- file.path(WORKSPACE_ROOT, "logs", OUTPUT_SUBDIR)
for (path in c(WORK_ROOT, OUTPUT_ROOT, LOG_ROOT)) {
  dir.create(path, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

PROJECT_PATH <- file.path(
  SPACING_ROOT, "src", "Spacing.Tool2", "Spacing.Tool2.csproj"
)
CONFIG_PATH <- file.path(SPACING_ROOT, "spacing.config.json")
DLL_DEBUG <- file.path(
  SPACING_ROOT, "src", "Spacing.Tool2", "bin", "Debug",
  TARGET_FRAMEWORK, "spacing-tool2.dll"
)
DLL_RELEASE <- file.path(
  SPACING_ROOT, "src", "Spacing.Tool2", "bin", "Release",
  TARGET_FRAMEWORK, "spacing-tool2.dll"
)
preferred_dll <- if (identical(tolower(BUILD_CONFIGURATION), "release")) {
  c(DLL_RELEASE, DLL_DEBUG)
} else {
  c(DLL_DEBUG, DLL_RELEASE)
}
existing_dll <- preferred_dll[file.exists(preferred_dll)]
TOOL2_DLL <- if (length(existing_dll)) {
  normalizePath(existing_dll[[1L]], winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
} else {
  NA_character_
}

HAS_LOCAL_RUNTIME <- file.exists(PROJECT_PATH) &&
  file.exists(CONFIG_PATH) && nzchar(Sys.which("dotnet")) &&
  !is.na(TOOL2_DLL)

if (RUN_MODELS && !HAS_LOCAL_RUNTIME) {
  stop(
    "Model execution is enabled, but the local runtime is incomplete. ",
    "Check the project, spacing.config.json, dotnet, and DLL. DLL paths checked: ",
    paste(preferred_dll, collapse = "; ")
  )
}

runtime_configuration <- data.frame(
  field = c(
    "rSpacing_version", "workspace_root", "rspacing_root", "spacing_root",
    "project_path", "config_path", "tool2_dll", "work_root",
    "output_root", "log_root", "run_models"
  ),
  value = c(
    as.character(utils::packageVersion("rSpacing")), WORKSPACE_ROOT,
    RSPACING_ROOT, SPACING_ROOT, PROJECT_PATH, CONFIG_PATH,
    if (is.na(TOOL2_DLL)) "NOT FOUND" else TOOL2_DLL,
    WORK_ROOT, OUTPUT_ROOT, LOG_ROOT, as.character(RUN_MODELS)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
utils::write.csv(
  runtime_configuration,
  file.path(LOG_ROOT, "runtime_configuration.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

APSIMX_TEMPLATE <- file.path(SPACING_ROOT, "examples", "template.apsimx")
result <- run <- cfg <- NULL
```

# Conventions

- Objects are built progressively and reused in subsequent chunks.
- Weather and geographic plots are available even without a model run.
- Output and soil plots are generated when `result` is available.
- Model-run chunks use `mock = TRUE` as the safe default.
- The `runs/`, `results/`, and `logs/` directories remain outside both Git repositories.
- `logs/manual_rev10/runtime_configuration.csv` records the effective runtime configuration.


# Resolved execution environment

The following table documents the paths actually used. With `run_models = false`, the DLL may be absent without preventing document rendering; with `run_models = true`, the project, configuration, `dotnet`, and DLL are required.

```{r runtime-configuration}
runtime_configuration
```

# Document configuration


## spacing_config()

**Purpose.** Demonstrates `spacing_config()` in the operational rSpacing workflow and explains where the function is used.

**Main inputs.** Uses the validated objects created in the preceding chunks and the arguments shown in the code example.

**Output and subsequent use.** Returns the object shown in the chunk, which is retained for validation, inspection, plotting, serialisation, or later workflow steps as appropriate.

Revision 10 runs the compiled `spacing-tool2.dll` (`use_compiled = TRUE`) instead of `dotnet run`, and gives Tool2 a copy of `spacing.config.json` whose weather and output folders are inside `runs/<output_subdir>/`, so that every file of the run stays in the workspace.

```{r f01-spacing_config}
if (HAS_LOCAL_RUNTIME) {
  tool2_settings <- jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(SPACING_ROOT, "spacing.config.json"))
  tool2_settings$TempWeatherDir <- file.path(WORK_ROOT, "tool2_weather")
  tool2_settings$OutputDir <- file.path(WORK_ROOT, "tool2_output")
  run_config_file <- file.path(WORK_ROOT, "spacing.config.json")
  jsonlite::write_json(tool2_settings, run_config_file, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)
  cfg <- spacing_config(
    apsim_dir = SPACING_ROOT,
    config_file = run_config_file,
    run_root = file.path(WORK_ROOT, "legacy-runs"),
    use_compiled = TRUE,
    executable = TOOL2_DLL
  )
} else cfg <- NULL
```

```{r f14-new_spacing_met}
met_data <- data.frame(
  date = dates, radn = 15 + 8 * sin(2 * pi * as.numeric(format(dates, "%j")) / 366),
  maxt = 20 + 10 * sin(2 * pi * (as.numeric(format(dates, "%j")) - 90) / 366),
  mint = 10 + 8 * sin(2 * pi * (as.numeric(format(dates, "%j")) - 90) / 366),
  rain = pmax(0, 2 + 2 * sin(2 * pi * as.numeric(format(dates, "%j")) / 31))
)

                       site = "Gualtieri demo")
```

# Robust selection of plotting variables

The daily and Report plotting functions of rSpacing require an explicit variable name. The following block selects an available numeric column while excluding dates and identifiers. The selected variable is shown in the document to make the plot reproducible and interpretable.

```{r select-plot-variables}
select_plot_variable <- function(data, preferred = character()) {
  if (is.null(data) || !is.data.frame(data) || !nrow(data)) return(NA_character_)
  numeric_names <- names(data)[vapply(data, is.numeric, logical(1))]
  numeric_names <- numeric_names[!grepl(
    "date|time|year|month|day|simulation|checkpoint|zone|clock|id$",
    numeric_names,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )]
  preferred_found <- preferred[preferred %in% numeric_names]
  if (length(preferred_found)) return(preferred_found[[1L]])
  if (length(numeric_names)) return(numeric_names[[1L]])
  NA_character_
}

daily_plot_variable <- select_plot_variable(
  daily,
  preferred = c("SoilCtot_kgCha", "N2O_total_kgNha", "LeachNO3_kgNha")
)
report_plot_variable <- select_plot_variable(
  report_table,
  preferred = c("Wheat_Yield_kgha", "Maize_Yield_kgha", "Soybean_Yield_kgha")
)

plot_variable_selection <- data.frame(
  source = c("daily", "report"),
  variable = c(daily_plot_variable, report_plot_variable),
  available = c(!is.na(daily_plot_variable), !is.na(report_plot_variable)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
plot_variable_selection
```

## plot_spacing_variable_panel()

**Purpose.** Demonstrates `plot_spacing_variable_panel()` in the operational rSpacing workflow and explains where the function is used.

**Main inputs.** Uses the validated objects created in the preceding chunks and the arguments shown in the code example.

**Output and subsequent use.** Returns the object shown in the chunk, which is retained for validation, inspection, plotting, serialisation, or later workflow steps as appropriate.

```{r f52-plot_spacing_variable_panel}
if (!is.null(result)) {
  dictionary <- spacing_variable_dictionary(result)

  # Use only variables that are numeric in an imported result table. The first
  # dictionary row may be a date such as Clock.Today and is therefore unsafe.
  numeric_daily <- if (is.data.frame(daily) && nrow(daily)) {
    names(daily)[vapply(daily, is.numeric, logical(1))]
  } else character()
  numeric_report <- if (is.data.frame(report_table) && nrow(report_table)) {
    names(report_table)[vapply(report_table, is.numeric, logical(1))]
  } else character()
  numeric_available <- unique(c(numeric_daily, numeric_report))
  numeric_available <- numeric_available[!grepl(
    "date|time|year|month|day|simulation|checkpoint|zone|clock|id$",
    numeric_available,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )]

  dictionary_variables <- if (
    is.data.frame(dictionary) && nrow(dictionary) &&
    "variable" %in% names(dictionary)
  ) {
    as.character(dictionary$variable)
  } else character()

  dictionary_numeric <- dictionary_variables[
    dictionary_variables %in% numeric_available
  ]
  preferred_variable <- c(
    daily_plot_variable,
    report_plot_variable,
    dictionary_numeric,
    numeric_available
  )
  preferred_variable <- preferred_variable[
    !is.na(preferred_variable) & nzchar(preferred_variable)
  ]
  variable_name <- if (length(preferred_variable)) {
    preferred_variable[[1L]]
  } else {
    NA_character_
  }

  variable_panel_selection <- data.frame(
    variable = variable_name,
    numeric_in_daily = !is.na(variable_name) && variable_name %in% numeric_daily,
    numeric_in_report = !is.na(variable_name) && variable_name %in% numeric_report,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  variable_panel_selection

  if (!is.na(variable_name)) {
    p_variable <- plot_spacing_variable_panel(
      result,
      variable = variable_name
    )
    print(p_variable)
  } else {
    message(
      "Variable panel skipped: no numeric non-identifier variable is available."
    )
  }
}
```

## plot_spacing_soil_profile()

**Purpose.** Demonstrates `plot_spacing_soil_profile()` in the operational rSpacing workflow and explains where the function is used.

**Main inputs.** Uses the validated objects created in the preceding chunks and the arguments shown in the code example.

**Output and subsequent use.** Returns the object shown in the chunk, which is retained for validation, inspection, plotting, serialisation, or later workflow steps as appropriate.

```{r f58-plot_spacing_soil_profile}
if (!is.null(result)) {
  # Layered APSIMx outputs are encoded as Variable(1), Variable(2), ... .
  # Derive the admissible base names from the imported tables instead of
  # assuming that the fixture exports a variable called exactly "SW".
  soil_source_tables <- Filter(
    function(x) is.data.frame(x) && nrow(x),
    list(daily = daily, report = report_table)
  )
  soil_column_names <- unique(unlist(
    lapply(soil_source_tables, names),
    use.names = FALSE
  ))
  indexed_columns <- soil_column_names[grepl(
    "\\([0-9]+\\)$",
    soil_column_names
  )]
  indexed_soil_variables <- unique(sub(
    "\\([0-9]+\\)$",
    "",
    indexed_columns
  ))

  # Prefer familiar water and nitrogen variables when they are genuinely
  # exported; otherwise use the first available indexed variable.
  preferred_soil_variables <- c(
    "SW", "Water.SW", "SoilWater.SW", "NO3", "NH4",
    "SoilC", "SoilCtot"
  )
  preferred_found <- preferred_soil_variables[
    preferred_soil_variables %in% indexed_soil_variables
  ]
  soil_window_variable <- if (length(preferred_found)) {
    preferred_found[[1L]]
  } else if (length(indexed_soil_variables)) {
    indexed_soil_variables[[1L]]
  } else {
    NA_character_
  }

  soil_variable_selection <- data.frame(
    selected_variable = soil_window_variable,
    indexed_variables_found = paste(indexed_soil_variables, collapse = "; "),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  soil_variable_selection

  if (!is.na(soil_window_variable)) {
    soil_plot_error <- NULL
    p_soil <- tryCatch(
      plot_spacing_soil_profile(
        result,
        variable = soil_window_variable,
        type = "time_depth"
      ),
      error = function(e) {
        soil_plot_error <<- conditionMessage(e)
        NULL
      }
    )
    if (!is.null(p_soil)) {
      print(p_soil)
    } else {
      message(
        "Soil profile plot skipped for '", soil_window_variable,
        "': ", soil_plot_error
      )
    }
  } else {
    message(
      "Soil profile plot skipped: the result contains no columns named ",
      "Variable(1), Variable(2), ... ."
    )
  }
}
```


## plot_spacing_soil_profiles()

**Purpose.** Demonstrates `plot_spacing_soil_profiles()` in the operational rSpacing workflow and explains where the function is used.

# Final audit

The final chunk verifies that the document contains a dedicated example for every exported function and summarises the objects created.

**What the final audit does.** It verifies that all public functions and S3 methods described in the manual are available in the installed namespace. It also reports the document version, local runtime availability, and model-run status.

```{r audit-finale}
exported_functions <- getNamespaceExports("rSpacing")
documented_exports <- c(
  "spacing_config", "validate_spacing_config", "new_spacing_request",
  "validate_spacing_request", "build_spacing_args", "run_spacing",
  "discover_spacing_outputs", "read_spacing_datastore", "read_spacing_csv",
  "read_spacing", "collect_spacing", "new_spacing_config_values",
  "read_spacing_config_file", "write_spacing_config_file",
  "update_spacing_config_file", "prepare_spacing_config_set",
  "prepare_spacing_runtime", "validate_spacing_config_values",
  "new_spacing_met", "prepare_spacing_met", "read_spacing_met",
  "write_spacing_met", "validate_spacing_met", "set_spacing_met_column",
  "remove_spacing_met_column", "set_spacing_met_constant",
  "subset_spacing_met", "spacing_met_default_units",
  "set_apsimx_weather_file", "spacing_daily", "spacing_report",
  "spacing_crop_summary", "spacing_units", "spacing_variable_unit",
  "classify_spacing_variables", "inventory_spacing_result",
  "plot_spacing_daily", "plot_spacing_report", "plot_spacing_result",
  "plot_spacing_daily_panel", "plot_spacing_report_panel",
  "plot_spacing_variable_panel", "plot_spacing_panels",
  "spacing_variable_dictionary", "describe_spacing_variable",
  "spacing_coordinates", "plot_spacing_location", "plot_spacing_map",
  "plot_spacing_met", "spacing_soil_layers", "plot_spacing_soil_profile",
  "plot_spacing_soil_profiles", "new_spacing_soil_spec",
  "new_spacing_cultivar_spec", "new_spacing_rotation_spec",
  "new_spacing_management_spec", "spacing_parameter_catalogue",
  "validate_spacing_parameters", "new_spacing_run_spec",
  "validate_spacing_run_spec", "write_spacing_run_spec",
  "read_spacing_run_spec", "update_spacing_parameters",
  "spacing_irrigation", "spacing_apply_irrigation",
  "spacing_fertiliser_application", "spacing_fertilisation",
  "spacing_apply_fertilisation", "spacing_cultivars",
  "spacing_validate_cultivar"
)
registered_s3_methods <- c(
  "print.spacing_config", "print.spacing_request", "print.spacing_run",
  "print.spacing_result", "plot.spacing_result", "plot.spacing_met",
  "print.spacing_run_spec", "as.list.spacing_irrigation",
  "print.spacing_irrigation", "summary.spacing_irrigation",
  "as.list.spacing_fertilisation", "print.spacing_fertilisation",
  "summary.spacing_result", "print.summary.spacing_result",
  "print.spacing_config_values", "print.spacing_runtime_setup",
  "print.spacing_met"
)

missing_exports <- setdiff(documented_exports, exported_functions)
registered_methods_found <- vapply(
  registered_s3_methods,
  function(method) exists(method, envir = asNamespace("rSpacing"), inherits = FALSE),
  logical(1)
)
stopifnot(length(missing_exports) == 0L)
stopifnot(all(registered_methods_found))

data.frame(
  exported_functions_documented = length(documented_exports),
  registered_s3_methods_documented = length(registered_s3_methods),
  local_runtime_available = HAS_LOCAL_RUNTIME,
  model_runs_enabled = RUN_MODELS,
  output_directory = OUTPUT_ROOT
)
```

# Expected outputs

When `run_models = true` and the model run completes successfully, the document shows daily data, reports, crop summaries, units, the variable dictionary, coordinates, maps, and all available plots. Objects built before the run, including weather, soil, cultivar, rotation, irrigation, fertilisation, and run specification, remain in the R session and can be saved with `saveRDS()`.


# Computation time

This manual performs zero APSIMx runs when `run_models = false` and one APSIMx run when `run_models = true`. The table below reports the measured model-run time and the total elapsed rendering time. Times depend on computer performance, storage speed, .NET warm-up, and whether dependencies have already been restored. The measured values from the target workstation should be used for planning; no fixed cross-computer duration is assumed.

```{r computation-time}
TOTAL_DOCUMENT_ELAPSED_SECONDS <- as.numeric(
  difftime(Sys.time(), DOCUMENT_STARTED_AT, units = "secs")
)
computation_time <- data.frame(
  mode = if (RUN_MODELS) "documentation plus one APSIMx run" else "documentation only",
  planned_APSIMx_runs = if (RUN_MODELS) 1L else 0L,
  measured_model_run_seconds = MODEL_RUN_ELAPSED_SECONDS,
  measured_total_render_seconds = TOTAL_DOCUMENT_ELAPSED_SECONDS,
  measured_total_render_minutes = TOTAL_DOCUMENT_ELAPSED_SECONDS / 60,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
computation_time
utils::write.csv(
  computation_time,
  file.path(LOG_ROOT, "computation_time.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
